Class Feistel

java.lang.Object
be.imgn.gaia.core.hash.Feistel
public final class Feistel extends Object
A Feistel network: a way to scramble the numbers of a given number of bits among themselves, that can be undone. Every number gives a different one, so that the numbers from zero to a power of two come out in another order, which the keys decide. 
var network = Feistel.of(32, key1, key2, key3, key4, key5, key6);
long scrambled = network.apply(42);          // some number below 2^32
network.invert(scrambled);                   // 42

It makes consecutive numbers, such as identifiers, look scattered, and gives them back; or visits a range in an order that looks random without storing it, as RandomPermutation does.

The number is split in two halves. Each round mixes one half, with a key, into the other one, then swaps them: since the half that is mixed in stays as it is, the round can be undone, whatever the mixing does. The mixing is Mixers.mix64(long).

How random the result looks depends on the numbers of bits and of rounds. Six rounds or more are advised. With very few bits, eight or so, the halves hold too few values to hide the structure, whatever the number of rounds: shuffle such a small range instead. It isn't cryptographic: someone who sees enough results finds the others.

Networks are immutable.

Since:
0.2.0
